findings.title: Google Meet bookings crash when destinationCalendar is missing
findings.body: The Google Meet fallback now reads mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration after destructuring evt.destinationCalendar ?? []. If the array is missing or empty (the new call sites pass null or []), mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws before any calendar event is created. The previous code used optional chaining (destinationCalendar?.integration), which fell back to Cal Video. Any Meet booking without a destination calendar now fails inside EventManager.create instead of booking.

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: referencesToCreate now sets credentialId only when the result type includes "_calendar", and forces undefined otherwise. Previously non-calendar results kept result.credentialId. Cancel (and any later video cleanup that looks up bookingReference.credentialId) will not find the Zoom/Daily/Meet credential, so the video meeting is left running after the booking is cancelled. New bookings created after this change are affected; updateLocation still copies result.credentialId, so the two paths disagree.

findings.title: Google organizer email is always the first destination calendar
findings.body: createEvent (and updateEvent) always uses destinationCalendar[0].externalId as the organizer attendee email, while the calendar written to is chosen by credentialId. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents calls createEvent once per host credential with the full array, so host 2's insert is authenticated as host 2 but marked organizer with host 1's calendar id. Google rejects that insert or creates the event under the wrong organizer, so secondary collective hosts do not get a correct event even on Google.

findings.title: Non-Google adapters still write only the first destination calendar
findings.body: CalendarManager now passes credential.id into createEvent so each host credential can target its own calendar, but Office 365 createEvent ignores that argument and always posts to destinationCalendar[0].externalId (or /me/calendar/events). Lark createEvent/updateEvent/deleteEvent (larkcalendar CalendarService.ts around line 129) and CalDAV createEvent (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts around line 162) do the same and only read index 0. For a second host, the request is made with that host's token against the first host's calendar id. Office/Lark fail the call; CalDAV filters to no calendars and still returns success, so the host silently gets no event. The collective multi-host fix therefore only works for Google.

findings.title: Collective host calendars are dropped when the organizer has none
findings.body: destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, and the collective branch then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). Optional chaining does not assign, so the array of other hosts' destination calendars is discarded. A collective event whose owner has no destination calendar creates no host calendar events at all, which is the case this PR is meant to fix. Initialize the array before pushing (for example evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]).

findings.title: Confirm and payment flows still pass a single destination calendar
findings.body: Only handleNewBooking appends every collective host's destinationCalendar before EventManager.create. confirm.handler, the Stripe webhook (packages/features/ee/payments/api/webhook.ts around lines 119 and 229), and the PayPal webhook (paypal-webhook.ts around line 152) still build evt.destinationCalendar from booking.destinationCalendar or the booking owner's calendar only. Collective events that require confirmation or payment create calendar events on that later path, so the other hosts never get a calendar event or a booking reference. Reschedule/cancel then have nothing to update for those hosts.

findings.title: Cancelling remaining recurring events only deletes the first calendar reference
findings.body: The new multi-reference loop wraps the recurring allRemainingBookings branch, but that branch still does updatedBookings references.find for a single _calendar reference and deletes it with every calendar credential on the booking owner, not with reference.credentialId. It also runs once per outer reference, so the same first event is deleted repeatedly. Other hosts' calendar events on the recurring series are never deleted, and a credential that does not own that event is used. Non-recurring cancel uses the per-reference credential and is fine; recurring collective cancel is not.

findings.title: One missing calendar credential aborts every calendar update
findings.body: updateAllCalendarEvents pushes updateEvent(credential, ...) even when credential is still undefined after the DB lookup (no row, or app.slug missing). getCalendar then throws inside the for-loop, before Promise.all and before later references are handled. The catch maps every calendar reference to success: false and no longer logs the error (console.error was removed), so a single bad host credential silently fails reschedule, location change, and attendee updates for every host.

findings.title: Google update no longer falls back to a destination calendar id
findings.body: updateEvent sets calendarId to externalCalendarId, or else find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId). When externalCalendarId is null or empty that comparison cannot match, so calendarId is undefined and events.update is called with no calendar id. The old code used destinationCalendar.externalId. Bookings whose references have no externalCalendarId (older rows, or creates that did not persist one) can no longer be rescheduled or updated on Google. deleteEvent has the same dead find, but still falls back to "primary"; update does not.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses an undefined calendar id
findings.body: Insert uses selectedCalendar || "primary", but the follow-up events.patch that writes the Meet link into the description passes calendarId: selectedCalendar with no fallback. selectedCalendar is undefined whenever no destination entry matches credentialId (or externalId is null). The event is created on primary and the patch is sent to an undefined calendar, so the description never gets the hangout link. Previously selectedCalendar was always an external id or "primary".

findings.title: Organization slug is stored under the opposite billing flag
findings.body: The spread was changed from !IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug } to IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}. That inverts org creation: self-hosted (billing disabled) organizations are created with no slug, so org URLs do not resolve, and billing-enabled organizations get slug set immediately instead of only requestedSlug pending approval. The requestedSlug line below was only rewritten from && to a ternary and is unchanged in meaning. This is unrelated to destination calendars and breaks org provisioning.

findings.title: Webhook destinationCalendar changed from object to array
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar is now DestinationCalendar[] | null, and BOOKING_* webhook payloads spread that field. Subscribers that read destinationCalendar.integration, .externalId, or .credentialId will break. The change is labeled a non-breaking bug fix. Payloads are also inconsistent: handleNewBooking still sends null when unset, while confirm/cancel/payment send []. The e2e fixture was only updated for BOOKING_REJECTED (null to []), so BOOKING_CREATED still expects null and does not lock the new array shape.
